items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: They told me that the other trumpet player whose name was Louis Hunt was having lip trouble... they had come to ask me if I would come to the theater and be on hand to do the next show if Hunt did not appear.

ctx.x: I was deep in slumberland when someone knocked on my door about 12.30 in the afternoon. It was the landlady of the rooming house where I was staying on 135th Street. My wife was working as a housemaid down town so I could sleep the whole day, so I had thought when I came home. The landlady told me that three men were at the hall door and wanted to see me. I told her to let them in. They were Gus McClung, Henry Goodwin and Residus 'Mac' Horton, three members of Cooper's orchestra. I had known Gus since the first…

They told me that the other trumpet player whose name was Louis Hunt was having lip trouble and felt so embarrassed because he had a feature number to do and had been missing the ending for a few days. So he did not show up for the first show and they had come to ask me if I would come to the theater and be on hand to do the next show if Hunt did not appear. I was so beat and knowing that I had to work with Russel that night, I told them I could not make it.

Two and a half hours later, Gus and Henry Goodwin came back this time with Paul Burnett, the ex-Arthur Gibbs guitarist. They told me that Hunt had not shown up for the second show and would I please come to do the last two ones. As it was the second time they had come for me, I told them 'yes' because my rest had been broken after the first visit
